keyWhy.en: The key ideas are the topic (scientists do not have one final answer about dreams, yet they have learned a great deal) and the conclusion (good sleep, including enough REM sleep, is important for learning, mood, and health). The green sentences are the answers.

qs.q: Why do we not act out our dreams during REM sleep?
qs.qko: 렘수면 중에 우리는 왜 꿈을 몸으로 따라 하지 않나요?
opts: Because the brain stops working during REM sleep
Because most of the body's muscles are temporarily relaxed
Because our eyes stay completely still
evs: Many of our most vivid dreams happen during a stage called REM sleep, which stands for rapid eye movement.
During REM sleep, the brain is highly active, but most of the body's muscles are temporarily relaxed, so we do not act out our dreams.
Every so often, the sleepers' eyes darted quickly back and forth under their closed eyelids.
In their view, dreams are simply a side effect of the brain's activity during sleep.
why: 렘수면 동안 뇌는 매우 활발하지만, 몸의 근육 대부분은 잠시 힘이 풀려 있어요. 그래서 꿈을 행동으로 옮기지 않아요.
During REM sleep, the brain is active, but most muscles are temporarily relaxed, so we do not act out our dreams.

qs.q: In the text, what does 'a side effect of the brain's activity' mean?
qs.qko: 글에서 'a side effect of the brain's activity(뇌 활동의 부수 효과)' 는 무슨 뜻인가요?
opts: An extra result that happens without a special purpose
A medicine that helps the brain sleep
A dangerous illness caused by dreaming
evs: One theory suggests that dreaming helps the brain store memories and connect new information with old knowledge.
Interestingly, some scientists argue that dreams may have no special purpose at all.
Sleep moves through cycles that last about 90 minutes.
Every night, most people spend around two hours dreaming, even if they remember nothing in the morning.
why: 바로 앞 문장에서 꿈에는 특별한 목적이 전혀 없을 수도 있다고 했어요. 목적 없이 그냥 따라서 생기는 결과라는 뜻이에요.
The sentence before says dreams may have no special purpose. A side effect is something that simply happens along with something else.

qs.q: Why might students who sleep well remember more than students who stay up all night?
qs.qko: 잠을 잘 잔 학생이 밤을 새운 학생보다 왜 더 많이 기억할 수 있나요?
opts: Because staying up all night makes dreams more vivid
Because tests are always easier in the morning
Because sleep and dreaming help the brain store memories and learn
evs: One theory suggests that dreaming helps the brain store memories and connect new information with old knowledge.
A third theory, sometimes called the threat simulation theory, says that dreams allow us to practice reacting to dangers safely.
Good sleep, including enough REM sleep, is important for learning, mood, and health.
In 1953, two researchers at the University of Chicago noticed something strange while watching people sleep.
why: 꿈이 뇌가 기억을 저장하도록 돕는다는 이론이 있고, 충분한 렘수면을 포함한 좋은 잠은 학습에 중요해요. 두 문장을 연결하면 답이 나와요.
One theory says dreaming helps the brain store memories, and good sleep is important for learning. Connect the two sentences.

ends: Why do some people know they are dreaming while they dream?
어떤 사람들은 왜 꿈속에서 자신이 꿈을 꾸고 있다는 걸 알까?
How much sleep do teenagers really need?
